facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s
history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and moderate pulmonary hypertension
presented with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and bilateral leg swelling
recurrent palpitations that occurred randomly and were often associated with shortness of breath
medications included aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, tiotropium, and a budesonide-formoterol inhaler
No specific physical examination findings were detailed in the case report
Left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% compared with 60% 2 months prior
25% narrowing of the left anterior descending artery and a distally occluded right coronary artery
Regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia with rate of 120 beats per minute
subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia
RR interval 800ms, PR interval 200ms
second PAC with prolonged PR interval of 390ms

concepts.why: The patient's history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, combined with the decreased left ventricular ejection fraction, suggests heart failure.
The patient's recurrent palpitations and the ECG findings of regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, combined with the findings of coronary artery narrowing and occlusion, suggests coronary artery disease.
The patient's history of COPD and symptoms of shortness of breath support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of moderate pulmonary hypertension and symptoms of shortness of breath support this diagnosis.
The patient's history of hypertension supports this diagnosis.
The patient's history of hyperlipidemia supports this diagnosis.
The ECG findings of subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia suggest atrial fibrillation.
It explains the prolonged PR interval of 200ms in sinus rhythm.
It explains the second PAC with a prolonged PR interval of 390ms.

rationales.F02: History of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and moderate pulmonary hypertension increases the likelihood of heart failure and coronary artery disease.
rationales.F03: Shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and bilateral leg swelling are symptoms commonly associated with heart failure.
rationales.F04: Recurrent palpitations are a symptom of supraventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F07: Left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% is a strong indicator of heart failure.
rationales.F08: 25% narrowing of the left anterior descending artery and a distally occluded right coronary artery are indicative of coronary artery disease.
rationales.F09: Regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia with a rate of 120 beats per minute is a characteristic finding of supraventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F10: Subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia are a characteristic finding of supraventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F11: RR interval of 800ms and PR interval of 200ms are within normal limits.
rationales.F12: Prolonged PR interval of 390ms is indicative of first-degree or second-degree atrioventricular block.
